Use case: style-transfer. SHAPE-LED ABSTRACT MATERIAL ART for actual Unity physics map "Tideway Metropolis". Input1 controls original whole-map positions, structure silhouettes, tower/low slab shapes, open voids, bridges, island outline, terrain and proportions. Input2 gives close construction details ONLY. User has REJECTED two failed approaches: uniform map skin packs AND pretending abstract open slab towers are literal offices/hotels/city buildings. DO NOT do either. These are interesting tactile sculptural worlds built on the ACTUAL open geometry.
Output THREE full-width stacked panels A/B/C. In each: main whole-map view at left occupying 75% width with all actual map structures, crop empty sky; right 25% has one macro-detail inset of an EXISTING pillar/deck joint, showing proposed texture and a few small attached visual embellishments. Keep same actual camera and structures across panels. Preserve original square slab outlines, levels, pillar fronts for climbing, holes, ramps and all bridge gaps. Polished playful Unity candy/toy art, not photoreal. Different structural shapes get visibly different material families WITHIN each scene: strong distinction between tall stacks, branching/folded forms and low open pavilions. Rich tactile texture, underside/edge/top differences and sparse small decorations are the focus, not functional building lore.
PANEL A TITLE "Weathered tide-strata". DETAILED SURFACE ASSIGNMENTS: Tall thin frame stacks: dark wet slate posts and pale opaque chalk tops, vivid turquoise mineral strata only on slab sides; center ring-capped stack: pearly cream posts with coral-orange side veins, a contrasting anchor. Branching slabs: green-blue nacre ripple patterns. Low courtyard and folded slabs: bleached timber grain with sand-polished edges and occasional small shell clusters on EXTERIOR corners. Bridges: neutral pale stone tops, tide-line bands on sides. A few short salt-crystal growths under OUTSIDE deck edges; no detail curtains. Warm sea mist, turquoise ocean, pale sandy island with flat tide-pattern textures.
PANEL B TITLE "Midnight liquid-metal playground". DETAILED SURFACE ASSIGNMENTS: Tall narrow stacks: charcoal posts and brushed silver opaque deck tops, irregular violet oil-slick slab SIDES and a few chunky chrome joint caps. Central ring stack: warm ivory speckled ceramic posts with magenta luminous hairline cracks; branching slabs: cyan anodized-metal sides with dark quiet tops. Low pavilions: peach/gray ceramic with large stipple patterns and sparse pink resin beads underneath outside corners. Do not put emission on every edge. Deep purple midnight sky with bright ambient fill, blue-black ocean, charcoal patterned island.
PANEL C TITLE "Amber root and polished mineral". DETAILED SURFACE ASSIGNMENTS: Central branching structures: rich grooved bark posts, amber-resin side plates with trapped bubble patterns; tall rear stacks: cool blue-gray basalt posts, ivory opaque top faces, turquoise quartz veins in sides. Ring-capped center stack: pale smooth wood and warm yellow translucent-looking resin SIDES, opaque tops. Low courts: warm clay ceramic with broad lichen patches and little dried seed-pod decorations under outside edges. Sparse curved root collars attached to a few exterior post bases, no vines over grip faces. Warm hazy dawn, moss/ochre island texture, muted green sea.
Add a few short material callouts beside macro inset, no fictional function labels. IMPORTANT: Sparse visual add-ons can be little shell clusters, seed pods, short hanging leaves, bolt caps, crystal nubs as specifically described. They cling to external non-walking edges and move with existing pieces conceptually; they must not become new structural supports or dense scenery. Do not add trees, giant fungus umbrellas, giant coral replacements, buildings, windows, walls, doors, platforms, railings, tent fabric, new terrain or separate islands. No literal book/office/shipyard props. No all-column single paint/color and no all-slab same finish. All walking tops opaque, quiet and readable, no fake holes. Lighting must retain readability even in dark scenes; avoid a point-light on every detail. Footer "AI SURFACE STUDIES • SHAPE REFERENCE, NOT UNITY CAPTURES".

Use case: style-transfer. Art-direction proof for actual Unity physics playground CANOPY BOROUGH. Attached image1 is actual whole-map geometry; image2 is the same map closeup. User explicitly rejected painting abstract structures as literal city buildings. DO NOT turn anything into an office, hotel, factory, house, temple, windowed building or believable urban architecture. These remain playful abstract OPEN STACKED SLABS, branching decks, rectangular pillars, bridges and low open pavilions. Preserve their exact silhouettes, positions, level counts, open voids and bridge connections.
Create one large polished concept board: THREE horizontal full-width panels, same actual whole-map angle in each with a small inset close detail to the right showing surfaces and very sparse attached details on an existing pillar/slab. Reduce empty sky, make structures large. Each panel explores a whole fantasy environment in which DIFFERENT STRUCTURAL SHAPES have contrasting tactile treatments AND a few lightweight visual embellishments. Avoid a uniform reskin. This is inspired stylized Unity game art, appealing candy-like specular control, NOT photoreal and NOT literal city design.
A. "AFTER THE GIANT RAIN". Central branching crowns have dark fibrous bark columns, broad deep jade slightly waxy deck TOPS with visible leaf veins; cream-to-coral undersides have sweeping mushroom GILL ridges as normal-map-like detail; floor plate outlines stay straight and unchanged. West branching cluster is drier reddish bark, golden top surfaces; east cluster is pale lichen bark and blue-green tops. Tall narrow skyline stack at rear center-right has contrasting dark wet black stone posts and small iridescent beetle-shell-like plates ATTACHED on outer column faces, not a facade filling gaps. Existing low folded terraces and courtyards are pale porous stone with velvety moss patches, occasional tiny mushroom clusters at outer corners and one or two curled leaves hanging just under OUTSIDE edges. All walking routes and handgrip pillar fronts remain clear. No new trees, giant mushrooms replacing blocks or hanging vine curtains. Deep lush green island TEXTURE, luminous warm overcast sky, teal sea; props sparse.
B. "THE REEF LEFT ABOVE WATER". Branching crowns become pearlescent shell-textured slab sides with radial nacre streaks; opaque pale blue-green walkable tops, warm pink gill-like undersides. Posts are porous coral-stone, NOT new coral shapes. The narrow tall skyline is contrasting dark basalt with fine cyan mineral veins and only a few attached barnacle clusters on OUTSIDE lower posts. Low pavilions are bleached driftwood-textured posts, pale sandstone floors with worn tide rings and shell flecks; a couple small kelp ribbons attached under exterior edges only. Central, west and east branch clusters differ in pearl, rust-pink, and smoky blue nacre. Keep all original abstract shapes, holes and bridges. Island is pale tidal mineral texture; clear aqua ocean, bright sea-mist sky. Sparse extra shell clusters accent existing joints; no coral forest.
C. "THE MAGNETIC PLAYTHING". Central branching slabs have smoky violet resin SIDES with embedded filament patterns, matte pale lilac walking tops and a few bead-sized chrome nodes attached to OUTSIDE joints; branch columns matte cream speckled ceramic. West branching structures use chunky yellow/orange molded plastic with broad swirl patterns; east use mint ceramic with cracked blue glaze. The tall rear skyline stack contrasts sleek graphite-coated columns, gray brushed deck tops, thin lime seams and one tiny copper coil shape on a few outward column faces. Low pavilions have warm peach/pale turquoise rubberized sides and visible chunky bolt-like corner decorations, restrained toy-scale texture, no literal architecture. Bridges have neutral opaque gray tops, colored side chips belonging to nearby clusters. Existing island becomes cool charcoal speckled rubber texture, ocean purple-blue and peach dusk sky. No extra floating platforms, no added walls.
Each panel needs at least three very visibly different tactile material families on different structure types WITHIN the same panel. Surface detail and a few external details carry the identity; no pretending structures serve city functions. Add only short small callouts: "leaf tops / gill undersides", "stone + shell plates", "mossed low slabs" in A; corresponding material names for B/C. Footer "AI VISUAL PROOF • ORIGINAL PLAYABLE SHAPES RETAINED AS REFERENCE".
